title: Moose Jaw Police Service introduces a New Opportunity for Students: ViPER Safety Patrol
content:
The Moose Jaw Police Service is excited to introduce a new opportunity for local students beginning or continuing post‑secondary studies this fall, who are interested in exploring a future in law enforcement and public safety.
This summer, we are launching the
ViPER (Visible Proactive Engagement Response) Safety Patrol
— a community‑focused initiative designed to give young people meaningful experience while helping keep Moose Jaw safe.
The ViPER program builds on a proven model developed by Chief Davis, who previously established
The Watch
in Lethbridge, Alberta — now celebrating its seventh year — as well as a Park Patrol program in Dryden, Ontario. These initiatives were inspired by innovative best practices he observed in Winnipeg, Vancouver, and Queensland, Australia.
“The ViPER is an opportunity for those considering a career in public safety to test the waters to see what aspects of public safety interest them.” Chief Davis said. “Ideally, we would like the ViPER to be a feeder league to a career in policing. But in my experience, some may realize that EMS, fire fighting, or social services appeals more to them – which is still a positive experience as it helps students select a career path and get exposure.”
As part of their role, ViPER team members will serve as additional eyes and ears for the Moose Jaw Police Service. They will support community safety initiatives such as Safe Walk, Visible Valuables, and bicycle safety programs. They will also assist with parking education and enforcement, and act as friendly ambassadors in Moose Jaw’s downtown.
Students interested in joining the ViPER Safety Patrol can apply online through the Moose Jaw Police Service website. Full program details and how to apply can be found on our website at
www.mjpolice.ca
.
We’re proud to offer this opportunity to local youth and look forward to the positive impact the ViPER Safety Patrol will have on our community.

title: STARS Lottery Scam
content:
To protect yourself, always keep these points in mind:
You will never be asked to send money to claim any lottery prize. If you are being asked to send a cheque, money order, or payment of any kind to claim your lottery prize, it is a scam. Hang up the phone or delete the email immediately. If you become suspicious, check with STARS directly to verify if you are a winner and if the lottery is legitimate.
In some instances, the fraudster has demanded payment via gift cards as a way to claim the prize. As a reminder, do not provide the scammer with the access codes for the gift cards under any circumstances.
The Moose Jaw Police Service would also like to remind the public not to provide personal information such as their Social Insurance Number (SIN), or banking details over the phone.
If you or someone you know has fallen victim to a scam, please get in touch with the Moose Jaw Police Service at 306-694-7600. If you prefer to remain anonymous, call the Moose Jaw Crime Stoppers with your information at 1-800-222-8477, go online at
p3tips.com, or download the mobile app.
For more information on fraud attempts, visit
Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre (antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca)

title: Can You Identify – Mischief Incident – UPDATE
content:
UPDATE:
The individual pictured has been identified.
————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————-
File # 2025-18376
The Moose Jaw Police Service is asking for the public’s assistance in identifying a male in connection with a mischief incident. On November 12, 2025, police responded to a report of an individual spray-painting or “tagging” a building on the 900 block of Home Street West. With video surveillance, police identified a young male in the area at the time of the incident.
The male was wearing all-black attire, with a white hat, and was carrying a skateboard. The male is a person of interest in an ongoing spray-painting incident.
Anyone with further information on the male suspect can contact CRIME STOPPERS at 1-800-222-8477 or the Moose Jaw Police Service at (306) 694-7600

title: ViPER Safety Patrol Commences Operations
content:
Moose Jaw Police Service’s newest team, the Visible Proactive Engagement Response (ViPER) Safety Patrol, has completed its training and will officially begin patrolling the streets of Moose Jaw this week.
Inspired by impactful initiatives in Winnipeg, Vancouver, and Queensland, Australia, and built from the blueprint of Chief Davis’s successful safety patrol programs in previous postings, the ViPER Safety Patrol offers young people interested in careers in law enforcement the opportunity to serve in a visible role while bolstering public safety in Moose Jaw.
This year’s ViPER team is comprised of four local Moose Jaw residents aspiring to careers in law enforcement: Wayne Bauluck, Aiden MacDonald, Haily Molde, and Kayden Lang.
“Between Crescent Park, the Public Library, and our many unique businesses and attractions, Moose Jaw has a vibrant downtown core, and the Moose Jaw Police Service is committed to keeping it safe,” said Chief of Police Rob Davis. “After working closely with these units over the past two weeks of training, I have the utmost confidence in their work ethic, dedication, and commitment to this city, and I look forward to the positive impact they will have in the community this summer.”
The ViPER Safety Patrol will serve as ambassadors for downtown Moose Jaw, reflecting strong partnership with local organizations, including Tourism Moose Jaw and the Downtown Moose Jaw Association. These units will also act as a visible extension of the Moose Jaw Police Service in key areas of the city, providing auxiliary services that promote public safety, such as Safe Walk programs, while also maintaining a vigilant presence to deter crime and support police operations. MJPS encourages residents to engage with these units while on patrol and to follow their work throughout the summer on social media.
The Moose Jaw Police Service’s mission is to serve as a community-focused safety agency, committed to peacekeeping, crime prevention, law enforcement, and community building.
The ViPER Safety Patrol was developed with this mission in mind and aligns closely with the three-year outcomes outlined in the Moose Jaw Police Service’s Strategic Map, including increased presence in high-risk areas, stronger connections with youth, expanded engagement at community events and in public spaces, and enhanced visibility throughout Moose Jaw.

title: Arrest – Moose Jaw Police Internet Child Exploitation Unit Investigation
content:
The Moose Jaw Police ICE Unit in partnership with the Saskatchewan Internet Child Exploitation Unit has charged a Moose Jaw man with child exploitation related offences.
On June 24, 2026, the Moose Jaw Police ICE Unit along with the Saskatchewan Internet Child Exploitation Unit executed a Search Warrant at a home in Moose Jaw, SK. Electronic devices were examined at scene and seized by investigators. Further, printed images of child exploitation related material were also located.
As a result of the investigation, 53-year-old Bradley Joseph Cournoyer was arrested and charged on June 24, 2026, with the following:
One count of Possessing Child Sexual Abuse and Exploitation Material
Further charges may result pending analysis of the seized electronic devices.
Cournoyer appeared in Moose Jaw Provincial Court on June 25, 2026 and was remanded into custody. His next court date is July 2, 2026.
(Court Information number: 991343143)
The Saskatchewan ICE Unit is comprised of investigators from the Saskatchewan RCMP, Regina Police and Saskatoon Police Service. Their mandate, along with Moose Jaw Police ICE Unit, is to investigate crimes involving Child Sexual Abuse and Exploitation Material.

title: Downtown Businesses’ Vigilance Leads to Counterfeit Arrest
content:
Starting on June 19, 2026, the Moose Jaw Police Service began receiving multiple reports of counterfeit currency being circulated throughout the city, culminating in an arrest on the afternoon of Sunday, June 21, 2026.
This arrest reflects a coordinated response between frontline business staff and members of the Moose Jaw Police Service. Police are highlighting this example as a demonstration of how police and the community can work together to protect the city.
Throughout the weekend, multiple businesses identified suspected counterfeit bank notes and promptly reported them to police. In one instance, an employee became suspicious after observing the suspect in possession of a large quantity of $50 and $100 bills. Police also noted that one of the targeted businesses had CCTV cameras positioned to capture the transaction, providing evidence that proved instrumental in identifying the suspect.
The information provided by businesses enabled investigators to identify a suspect, obtain a warrant for his arrest, and distribute his description to officers.
Police Chief Robert Davis, who was off duty at the time, observed an individual matching the description of the suspect in public and maintained visual contact until patrol officers were able to attend the scene and arrest the 36-year-old male. The suspect was subsequently charged with Possession of Counterfeit Money and Uttering Counterfeit Money.
“One of Moose Jaw Police Service’s core values is working together with our community, and this investigation is a strong example of that partnership in action,” said Zach Bachmann, Public Information Manager. “The vigilance and cooperation of the businesses involved were instrumental in this investigation and helped prevent additional businesses from being victimized.”
Moose Jaw Police Service encourages businesses to consider the measures that contributed to this investigation, including ensuring employees are attentive when handling currency, prepared to report suspicious activity, and supported by effective monitoring systems. Members of the public and businesses who suspect they have received counterfeit currency should avoid recirculating it and contact police immediately. Additional information on identifying counterfeit currency and the security features of Canadian bank notes is available through the Bank of Canada’s Counterfeit Prevention resources.

title: Moose Jaw Police Service Swears in Five New Officers
content:
On Thursday, July 9, 2026, the Moose Jaw Police Service, together with the Moose Jaw Board of Police Commissioners, swore in five new officers during a ceremony held at the Moose Jaw Public Library’s Performing Arts Theatre. In attendance were local MLAs, representatives from local organizations, the Chief Marshal of the Saskatchewan Marshal Service, and the Minister of Community Safety.
The Honourable David Chow, Judge of the Provincial Court of Saskatchewan, administered oaths to Constable Joel Robinson, Brett Weichel, Taylor Mazenc,
Jasveer Singh, and Geoffrey LaBuick at this ceremony.
Cst. Robinson joined the MJPS on June 1, 2026, after previously serving with the Saskatchewan Highway Patrol. Recruits Weichel, Mazenc, Singh, and LaBuick will begin training at the Saskatchewan Police College later this month.
When asked what inspired them to pursue a career in policing with the Moose Jaw Police Service, the recruits shared the following:
Regina native Brett Weichel said:
“I’ve wanted to become a police officer for most of my life. As I started to work more in my career, more and more, I became that person—helping people out in their vulnerable times and responding to emergencies. I wanted to continue doing that in a larger setting and advance my career.”
He went on to say:
“I’m a person who likes to be challenged and pushed, and I think that Police College is going to be a great place for me to be able to do that, as well as learn from current officers and officers that have served in the past that have got the years of wisdom and experience to pass on to us.”
Taylor Mazenc, a long-time Moose Jaw resident, said:
“I chose to pursue a career with the Moose Jaw Police Service because I believe deeply in the responsibility citizens share to strengthen their community. Rather than simply benefiting from Moose Jaw, I am committed to contributing to what makes it an exceptional place to live.”
Mazenc added:
“I look forward to Police College as an opportunity to sharpen my skills, build effective teamwork, and grow as a reliable and capable individual.”
Jasveer Singh, who established roots in Moose Jaw after immigrating to Canada, said:
“I have always been driven by a desire to help others, and policing gives me the opportunity to make a lasting, positive impact in the community every day. Moose Jaw welcomed me with kindness and a strong sense of community, and it is the place where I built the foundation of my life in Canada.”
Born and raised in Moose Jaw, Geoffrey LaBuick said:
“I knew I wanted to be a cop since Grade 11.”
He added:
“I couldn’t be happier with being selected. The fact that I get to do it in my home community means everything to me.”
The ceremony also provided an opportunity to recognize current and former members of the Moose Jaw Police Service for promotions, retirement milestones, service recognition, and exemplary service through plaques presented by Chief of Police, Robert Davis.
Members recognized for recent promotions included Sergeant Shawn Mohle, who was promoted on January 20, 2025, and Superintendents Trish Seman and Randy Boechler, who were promoted on January 15, 2025. These promotions reflect decades of experience, leadership, and service across a wide range of roles. The Moose Jaw Police Service also acknowledges Sergeant Jay Sills and Staff Sergeants Jason Watt and Ryan Lawrence, who were unable to attend the ceremony but were also recognized for their recent promotions.
The Moose Jaw Police Service also recognized Jay-D Haughton for his service as Public Information and Strategic Communications Manager from September 2023 to April 2026. Through his work supporting organizational communications, media relations, and community engagement, Haughton made valuable contributions to the MJPS and helped strengthen communication and engagement with the community.
Plaques were also presented to honour the distinguished careers of Marlie Frei and Murray Rice as they concluded their service with the Moose Jaw Police Service. Together, Frei and Rice dedicated approximately 50 years of service across a variety of roles and demonstrated a steadfast commitment to keeping Moose Jaw safe with professionalism and integrity.
Chief Davis also recognized Superintendent Rick McKenna, recipient of the Police Exemplary Service Medal in recognition of 40 years of exemplary service. Since joining the Moose Jaw Police Service in 1985, Supt. McKenna has served in numerous operational and leadership roles, leaving a lasting impact on the organization through his dedication, professionalism, and commitment to serving the community.

title: Police Renew Appeal for Information on Missing Travis Perlman One Year After His Disappearance
content:
The Moose Jaw Police Service is renewing its appeal to the public for information regarding the disappearance of 20-year-old Travis Perlman.
Travis was last known to be in Moose Jaw on August 7, 2025, and was reported missing to police on September 7, 2025.
He was last seen wearing a dark-colored Nike zip-up sweater with a green logo and grey Timberland boots. He is described as 5’8” tall, weighing between 130 and 140 pounds, with brown hair and blue eyes. He also has a distinctive spider and skull tattoo on his left forearm.
This investigation remains a top priority for the Moose Jaw Police Service. Police have investigated numerous leads and partnered with agencies in multiple jurisdictions across Western Canada to determine Mr. Perlman’s whereabouts and the circumstances surrounding his disappearance.
Despite these extensive efforts, Mr. Perlman remains missing and his whereabouts are unknown.
The Moose Jaw Police Service remains committed to pursuing every available investigative avenue to determine the circumstances surrounding this disappearance.
The Moose Jaw Police Service asks the public to take another look at his photograph, share this appeal, and contact police if they have any information that may assist investigators.
No piece of information is too small; even seemingly insignificant details may assist investigators.
Anyone with information is asked to contact the Moose Jaw Police Service at 306-694-7600. Anonymous tips can also be submitted through Crime Stoppers online or by calling 1-800-222-8477.
